# Swarm stack and managed-agent platform engineering

Use for implementation, diagnosis, review, and release work across Swarm and applications embedding its managed-agent runtime. Route by subsystem, trace behavior end to end, preserve unrelated changes, and verify progressively with focused tests, race tests, builds, rendered UI, and harmless live probes.

## Repository and verification discipline
Confirm root, branch, remotes, dirty state, and canonical implementation tree before editing. Process artifacts are evidence, not production dependencies. Validate package-local changes first, then affected modules and live behavior. Never infer runtime success from compilation, provider availability from a catalog, or UI correctness without rendered evidence.

## Durable autonomous pipelines
Read the ledger/tracker first and preserve append-only decisions, blockers, dependency order, unrelated WIP, and disjoint ownership. Dispatch bounded workers with exact scopes and acceptance criteria; reviewers independently inspect diffs and gates. Reconstruct interrupted work from ledger, HEAD, processes, locks, artifacts, and logs before restarting. Use detached tmux only when jobs must survive tool reaping, poll readiness, and keep credentials out of logs. Completion requires durable artifacts, exact gates, no active task states, and an explicit next step or blocker.

## TUI, settings, providers, and context
Keep raw message coordinates distinct from wrapped visual coordinates; use ANSI/grapheme-aware wrapping, stable IDs, deterministic sorting, and symmetric anchor conversions. Mirror settings through schema, constructors, reload, persistence, navigation, and migrations. Key model overrides by normalized provider/model. After compaction reset live-context counters rather than cumulative telemetry.

Trace provider behavior through catalog → identity → credential resolver/vault → factory → request translation → stream normalization → usage/persistence → UI. Preserve routing precedence, redact and atomically store credentials, synchronize shared providers, reconcile stream events by stable identity, and prevent cache/input double counting. Classify auth, entitlement, model, rate-limit, and transport failures separately. Layered credential stores need a non-nil fallback for every unconditional traversal; UI “unlocked” state does not prove every storage path is safe.

## Protocols, tools, agents, and persistence
Treat authoritative SDK schemas as protocol contracts; verify versions, discriminators, field names, permissions, and real probes. Keep launcher connectivity separate from providers, tools, credentials, and permissions. Distinguish tool registration, filtering, reachability, invocation, and successful outcome. Centralize sandbox predicates, make rollback exhaustive, deep-copy asynchronous observations, and complete cancellation safely. Persist conversations, schedules, and tasks with explicit identities, SQLite WAL, default-deny authorization, restart-safe IDs, coherent events/conversions, and race-safe voice lifecycle.

## Joining independent hook enforcement gates
When hooks independently gate the same tool stream, compare exemption predicates side by side before changing priority. Extract shared tool classifiers into the lowest cycle-safe package and retain thin local wrappers when that minimizes churn. Gate one hook’s clock on the other hook’s actual success condition, preferably sticky after first success and fail-open only when the dependency is unavailable. Re-anchor count-based nudges to meaningful lifecycle events; account for the triggering call’s own increment.
